chunks: All praise is due to Allah, even though time has brought (for us) crushing calamity and great occurrence.

And I stand witness that there is no god but Allah, the One, there is no partner for Him nor is there with Him any god other than Himself, and that Muhammad is His slave and His Prophet (May Allah’s blessing and greeting be upon him and his progeny).

key_terms.الدهر: Time or age, often referring to the passage of time and its events
key_terms.توحيد: Divine unity (implied by 'La ilaha illa Allah')
key_terms.صلى الله عليه وآله: Peace be upon him and his family (SAWW)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of the opening declaration in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This opening Fatiha of Nahj al-Balagha, delivered by Imam Ali (AS) after the Battle of Siffin, poetically acknowledges divine decree amidst the political turmoil of arbitration (Hukm). It establishes the theological baseline of Tawhid and Nubuwwah, grounding the subsequent rhetorical arguments in the certainty of God's sovereignty despite human conflict. This declaration reflects the Shia scholarly view of Imam Ali as the embodiment of patience (Sabr) and wisdom during times of trial.
